subject: Sensitive-field indexing & erase policy — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@acuvera.com>
Cc: Lina Morales <lina.morales@acuvera.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Sensitive-field indexing & erase policy — follow-up and next steps

Hi Rajesh —

Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so the team is aligned and we can move toward a pilot scope: 

- Current flow: Acuvera sends user requests to your API gateway -> Redwood forwards to selected LLM model for feature flags and triage -> request/response logs stored in your GCP project (logging topic: projects/acuvera-logs).
- Primary concerns you raised: 1) which fields in request/response logs must be redacted vs indexed for observability, 2) retention/erase policy for PII, and 3) whether trace IDs or headers can be pseudonymized instead of removed to preserve debugging.

Immediate asks I have from the call:
1) Can you share the data map with the list of request/response fields (we discussed a sample subset) — you mentioned an internal spreadsheet.
2) Clarify your regulatory retention target (HIPAA retention is a concern for a small subset of logs) — you said 30/90/365 buckets?
3) Confirm which teams need search/indexing vs which need read-only audit access (ops vs security).

I’m attaching a short summary of redaction options we discussed and a template we can use for the pilot. Proposed next steps:
- You drop the data-map (acuvera-data-map.xlsx) into the Drive folder I shared.
- Karthik and I will propose an approach with three options: remove-sensitive-fields, hash-traceids+tokenize-headers, and indexed-with-policy (only allow hashed id + audit access).
- Quick pilot: 2-week ingest of non-prod traffic into a sandbox cluster with field-level redaction active.

Can you confirm the data-map and preferred retention buckets by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks —
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@acuvera.com>

Cc: Lina Morales <lina.morales@acuvera.com>, Security <security@acuvera.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sensitive-field indexing & erase policy — follow-up and next steps

Irene — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications inline: 

- Data map: attaching the spreadsheet (acuvera-data-map.xlsx) — it has a tab for request headers, request body, and response body. Note: we intentionally keep "patient_id" and "encounter_id" as indexed for product telemetry, but they must be hashed for any external systems.
- Retention: security wants 30 days for operational logs, 365 days for audit logs (policy exception for billing events at 7 years).
- Teams: Ops needs indexed search on error_code, route, and the hashed patient_id. Security wants raw audit trails accessible only via an export request (with IAM gate).

Regarding trace IDs: we prefer pseudonymization (HMAC with rotating key) over complete stripping so debugability in correlation is preserved. Can Redwood support rotating keys or do you require static salt?

Attaching the data map. Also looping in Lina for the legal/controls question — Lina, can you confirm the retention alignment?

Thanks,
Rajesh

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sensitive-field indexing & erase policy — follow-up and next steps

Irene — read the data map Rajesh sent. Quick tech notes for the proposed options: 

1) remove-sensitive-fields: easy to implement at the ingress filter level. Will increase false negatives in observability when patient_id is used for grouping.

2) hash-traceid + tokenize-headers: we can HMAC trace IDs with a per-customer rotating HMAC key; rotation requires key rollover support and a short grace period for cache reconciliation. We can store key metadata in the customer vault (KMS/HSM) and provide an API for rotation.

3) indexed-with-policy: we can index a normalized, truncated patient_id (e.g., first 8 chars of SHA256) for low-cardinality metrics and keep the full hashed value with restricted access. That preserves most search queries while limiting exposure.

Technical caveats: hashed patient_id will still be linkable across systems if the same hashing scheme is used externally; we should recommend salted HMAC with a secret managed by Acuvera. Also need to confirm downstream analytics ingestion to ensure no re-identification.

I'll draft a short options doc and propose the pilot config (sandbox ingest -> transform -> index) by tomorrow morning.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Lina Morales <lina.morales@acuvera.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sensitive-field indexing & erase policy — follow-up and next steps

Rajesh / Lina — thanks for the map and quick confirmation. Summary + agreed next steps below so everyone has the action items: 

Agreed scope for pilot (sandbox, 2 weeks):
- Ingest: non-prod request/response stream from Acuvera (redwood.sandbox.acuvera)
- Transform: field-level policies applied at ingress: hash(patient_id) with HMAC rotation, strip Social Security Number and full DOB, redact any free-text PII per regex
- Indexing: index error_code, route, and truncated-hash(patient_id) (first 8 hex chars) for ops queries
- Retention: operational logs 30 days (hot tier), audit logs retained 365 days in a colder tier with export-only access

Action items: 
- Rajesh: confirm the KMS plan for HMAC rotation and drop final XLSX into the shared Drive (done).
- Lina: confirm legal retention exception for billing events by Friday (cc’d).
- Karthik: provide the sandbox config + redaction pipeline spec and a proposed key-rotation timeline by EOD tomorrow.
- Irene/Monica: prep a short SOW addendum for pilot (estimated 2 engineer-weeks) and provide a pricing placeholder for the sandbox run.

Attachments: redaction-options-summary.pdf (summary of the three approaches).

If that all looks right I’ll schedule the kickoff next Monday at 10am PST for a 30-min alignment and start the SOW draft.

Best,
Irene
